title: Diabetic retinopathy detection from fundus photographs
summary: A two-track image classification competition — build a CNN from scratch, and fine-tune a pretrained one. Best models scored 0.780 and 0.826 AUC.
context: Private Codabench competition run as coursework (MSc); no public leaderboard to link to

sections.heading: The problem
body: Detect diabetic retinopathy from fundus photographs. Original labels: a 0-4 clinical severity scale, collapsed to binary for the competition (73/27 class split).
list: 2,000 training / 500 validation / 1,000 test images, across two tracks: train a CNN from scratch, or fine-tune an ImageNet backbone
Constant risk on both tracks: overfitting on only 2,000 training images

sections.heading: Approach
body: Shared preprocessing: unify orientation, crop to the retinal disc, Ben Graham contrast normalisation. Class imbalance handled twice — weighted loss and a weighted sampler.

images.alt: Original fundus photograph next to the same image after Ben Graham contrast normalisation
images.caption: Original vs. after Ben Graham contrast normalisation — vessels and small lesions become far more visible to the network.

list: 380px instead of the usual 224 on the fine-tuning track — microaneurysms, the main early signal, are small
±180° rotation instead of ±15° — fundus cameras have no fixed orientation, so the narrow range throws away most valid rotations
From-scratch track: 5-block CNN, ~1M params, averaged over 3 seeds
Fine-tuning track: weighted ensemble of DenseNet121, DenseNet169, ResNeXt50 — unfrozen in two stages, ensemble weights via grid search

sections.heading: Result
body: 0.826 AUC (fine-tuning) / 0.780 AUC (from-scratch) on the private test set.

images.alt: Bar chart of private-set AUC for every submission across both tracks; the lowest bar is a dtype bug that turned every image grey
images.caption: Every submission, both tracks. Private-set AUC — the bottom bar on the left is a dtype bug that turned every image grey.

sections.heading: What didn't work
list: CLAHE broke the crop step by changing the global intensity the crop depended on
A dtype bug in contrast normalisation turned every image grey — sent results below baseline until found
SE blocks + residual connections on the custom CNN overfit immediately
±180° augmentation that helped pretrained models failed completely from scratch (0.53 AUC)
Unfreezing a third DenseNet block overfit — two stages was the right place to stop
Dropped a 4th backbone (SE-ResNeXt50) from the ensemble — correlated too closely with ResNeXt50 to add value
